context.title: The Spirit Comes at Pentecost
context.summary: At Pentecost the Spirit comes with wind and fire, and the believers speak in other languages. Peter preaches Jesus crucified and risen, about three thousand are baptized, and a new community forms.
context.background: Pentecost, the Feast of Weeks, came fifty days after Passover and celebrated the grain harvest (Leviticus 23:15-21). It was a pilgrimage feast, so Jews from across the known world were in Jerusalem, which explains the long list of nations (vv. 9–11).

customs.note: About 9 a.m. Peter points out it is far too early in the day for the crowd to be drunk.

watchFor: Peter quotes Joel 2, Psalm 16 and Psalm 110.
'Repent, and be baptized every one of you' (v. 38).
Four marks of the community: teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, prayers (v. 42).

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Joel
people.summary: The second of the twelve minor prophets. He was the son of Pethuel.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Asia
places.summary: Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts 19:26, 27; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2.

places.name: Cappadocia
places.summary: The easternmost and the largest province of Asia Minor. Christianity very early penetrated into this country (1 Pet. 1:1).

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Mesopotamia
places.summary: The country between the two rivers (Heb. Aram-naharaim; i.e., “Syria of the two rivers”), the name given by the Greeks and Romans to the region between the Euphrates and the Tigris (Gen. 24:10; Deut. 23:4; Judg. 3:8, 10).

places.name: Pontus
places.summary: A province of Asia Minor, stretching along the southern coast of the Euxine Sea, corresponding nearly to the modern province of Trebizond. In the time of the apostles it was a Roman province.

places.name: Cyrene
places.summary: A city (now Tripoli) in Upper Libya, North Africa, founded by a colony of Greeks (B.C. 630). It contained latterly a large number of Jews, who were introduced into the city by Ptolemy, the son of Lagus, because he thought they would contribute to the security of the place.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Libya
places.summary: The country of the Ludim (Gen. 10:13), Northern Africa, a large tract lying along the Mediterranean, to the west of Egypt (Acts 2:10).

places.name: Pamphylia
places.summary: Paul and his company, loosing from Paphos, sailed north-west and came to Perga, the capital of Pamphylia (Acts 13:13, 14), a province about the middle of the southern sea-board of Asia Minor.

places.name: Phrygia
places.summary: Dry, an irregular and ill-defined district in Asia Minor. It was divided into two parts, the Greater Phrygia on the south, and the Lesser Phrygia on the west.

places.name: Rome
places.summary: The most celebrated city in the world at the time of Christ. It is said to have been founded B.C. 753. When the New Testament was written, Rome was enriched and adorned with the spoils of the world, and contained a population estimated at 1,200,000, of which the half were slaves, and including representatives of nearly every nation then known.

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

events.title: The Holy Spirit comes
events.summary: Passage: Acts 2:1–13. People: God, Holy Spirit. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Peter preaches at Pentecost
events.summary: Passage: Acts 2:14–41. People: Simon. Place: Jerusalem.
